desc:
Each cell of the rectangular grid has a non-negative toll. You travel from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down, and normally pay the toll of every cell you stand on, including the first and the last one.

You also own k waiver tickets. A ticket can be used on any cell of your route to pay nothing for that cell; at most one ticket per cell, and you do not have to use them all. Return the smallest total toll that you can be charged.
hints: Without tickets this is the plain minimum path sum. A ticket is a limited resource, so the best choice at a cell depends on how many tickets are still left.
Add a dimension: f[j][r][c] is the cheapest cost of reaching (r, c) having used exactly j tickets so far.

Entering cell (r, c) from a neighbour, either pay grid[r][c] and keep j, or waive it and come from the neighbour's state j - 1. Take the minimum over both options and both neighbours; the answer is the minimum over all j at the last cell.
editorial: A route together with a choice of cells to waive is all that matters, and the waived cells will obviously be the most expensive ones on the route. That observation gives a quick brute force, but for a DP it is easier to decide cell by cell. Let f[j][r][c] be the cheapest total for a route that ends at (r, c) and has used exactly j waivers on its cells so far.

To enter (r, c) with j waivers used, there are two options: pay for the cell and arrive with the same j from the upper or left neighbour, or waive it and arrive with j - 1 from either neighbour at no extra cost. Using fewer than k tickets is allowed, so the result is the minimum of f[j][m-1][n-1] over j from 0 to k. This takes O(k · m · n) time and O(k · n) space with a rolling row, which is tiny for k ≤ 10.
